SR-001.justification: 1 000 single and batched sends return exactly the announced ids; after an etf refusal the next 10 frames carry the ids announced for them, on all three receive paths in CI.

SR-002.justification: Exhaustive over tx_type 0..=3, rx_filter 0..=15 and all requests: writes only widen rx NONE to ALL and tx OFF to ON.

SR-003.justification: 2 000 unread stamps: recv waits about 200 ms with little CPU, at most 1 024 are queued, timestamps_lost counts the rest.

SR-004.justification: Through etf one refused launch time gives invalid = 1 and every sent frame keeps its timestamp, reading tx_errors and timestamps in either order.

SR-005.justification: Every payload is read through the checked cmsg reader; short and truncated control messages are skipped; the classifier counts only launch-time origins.

SR-006.evidence: src/sys/bsd.rs open: tx_timestamping returns Unsupported naming transmit timestamps
SR-006.justification: The BSD backend refuses tx_timestamping with ErrorKind::Unsupported and a message naming it; compiled and linted for macOS and FreeBSD in CI.
